CAR precision matrix of an adjacency graph

Source: R/marginal_se_spatial.R
tulpa_car_precision_Q.Rd

The conditional autoregressive precision Q = tau * (D - rho * W), with W the adjacency matrix and D the diagonal matrix of neighbour counts. At rho = 1 it is the intrinsic (ICAR) precision, the graph Laplacian, whose null space holds one constant direction per connected component; it is returned without an identifying augmentation, so a caller imposes the sum-to-zero constraints itself. For rho strictly inside the range set by the eigenvalues of D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2} (in particular 0 <= rho < 1 on a graph without isolated nodes) it is a proper, full-rank precision.

Usage

tulpa_car_precision_Q(adjacency, rho = 1, tau = 1)

Arguments

adjacency

Square symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix (dense or sparse).

rho

Spatial dependence parameter.

tau

Precision scale.

Value

A sparse symmetric precision matrix (dsCMatrix).

See also

spatial_car(), spatial_car_proper(), tulpa_latent_ascent()

Examples

A <- matrix(0, 4, 4); A[cbind(1:3, 2:4)] <- 1; A <- A + t(A)
tulpa_car_precision_Q(A)              # path-graph Laplacian
#> 4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dsCMatrix"
#>                 
#> [1,]  1 -1  .  .
#> [2,] -1  2 -1  .
#> [3,]  . -1  2 -1
#> [4,]  .  . -1  1
tulpa_car_precision_Q(A, rho = 0.9)   # proper CAR
#> 4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dsCMatrix"
#>                         
#> [1,]  1.0 -0.9  .    .  
#> [2,] -0.9  2.0 -0.9  .  
#> [3,]  .   -0.9  2.0 -0.9
#> [4,]  .    .   -0.9  1.0
